en: Udāna 7.9 Udapānasutta Thus have I heard:
On one occasion, while the Blessed One was wandering on tour among the Mallas with a large community of monks, he arrived at a brahmin village of the Mallas named Thūṇa.
The brahmin householders of Thūṇa heard:
"Friends, the ascetic Gotama, the son of the Sakyans who went forth from the Sakyan clan, has been wandering on tour among the Mallas with a large community of monks and has now arrived at Thūṇa."
They filled the well with grass and chaff right up to the brim, thinking:
"Lest those shaven-headed little ascetics drink the water.
Then the Blessed One, having stepped down from the road, approached the foot of a tree; having arrived, he sat down on the prepared seat.
Having sat down, the Blessed One addressed the Venerable Ānanda:
“Come now, Ānanda, fetch me some water from this well.
When this was said, the Venerable Ānanda said this to the Blessed One:
“Venerable sir, that well has now been filled with grass and chaff right up to the brim by the brahmin householders of Thūṇeyyaka, [thinking]:
‘Lest those shaven-headed ascetics drink our water.
A second time... [as before]...
A third time the Blessed One addressed the Venerable Ānanda:
“Come now, Ānanda, fetch me some water from this well.
“Very well, Bhante,” the Venerable Ānanda replied to the Blessed One, and taking his bowl, he went to that well.
Then, as the Venerable Ānanda approached, that well vomited out all its grass and chaff from its mouth and stood as if overflowing,
filled to the brim with clear, untroubled, and serene water.
Then this thought occurred to the Venerable Ānanda:
“It is wonderful, indeed, sir! It is marvelous, indeed, sir! How great is the psychic power and majesty of the Tathāgata!
For when I approached this well, it emptied out all that grass and chaff from its mouth and stood as if overflowing, filled to the brim with clear, undisturbed, and serene water.
Taking drinking water in his bowl, he approached the Blessed One and, having approached, said this to the Blessed One:
“It is wonderful, Bhante! It is marvelous, Bhante! Such is the great psychic power and great majesty of the Tathāgata.
For when I approached, Bhante, this well—having vomited out all that grass and chaff from its mouth—stood as if overflowing, filled to the brim with clear, undisturbed, and serene water.
Let the Blessed One drink the water; let the Sugata drink the water.”
Then the Blessed One, having understood this matter, on that occasion uttered this inspired exclamation:
“What need is there for a well,
if water were always present?
Having cut craving at its root,
why would one pursue the search? Thus ends the ninth [verse].
